title: ‘Varuvaaiy’ Becomes First Tamil Song Ever Nominated for a Grammy Award
excerpt: Devan Ekambaram and Susha’s contemporary setting of a Subramania Bharati devotional poem is shortlisted for Best Global Music Performance at the 69th Grammys, alongside Shakira, Burna Boy and Rosalía.
body:
• “Varuvaaiy,” composed by Indian American musician Devan Ekambaram and featuring vocalist Susha, has been nominated for Best Global Music Performance at the 69th Grammy Awards — the first Tamil song ever to receive a Grammy nomination.
  • The track is a contemporary setting of a devotional poem by Subramania Bharati, the Tamil poet and freedom fighter, blending Carnatic music with modern instrumentation.
  • It competes against entries featuring Angélique Kidjo, Pharrell Williams, Shakira, Burna Boy and Rosalía.
  • The winners will be announced on February 7, 2027, at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles.

A Tamil bhajan has done what no Tamil song has done before. When the Recording Academy announced the nominations for the 69th Grammy Awards on November 16, “Varuvaaiy” — a contemporary interpretation of a century-old devotional poem by Subramania Bharati — was named in the Best Global Music Performance category, becoming the first Tamil-language song ever nominated for a Grammy, according to The Hollywood Reporter India. It is the first Grammy nomination for both of its artists: composer-singer Devan Ekambaram, who was born and raised in the United States, and vocalist Subhiksha Rangarajan, known professionally as Susha.

A Bharati poem, set to raag Desh

Bharati’s poem, written over a century ago, is a devotional composition dedicated to Lord Krishna, invoking the deity to descend into the human intellect and destroy evil. Ekambaram has reimagined it through a blend of Carnatic classical music and contemporary instrumentation, with the composition drawing on raag Desh. The poem has been part of the Carnatic repertoire for generations; Bharati is believed to have written it during his exile in Pondicherry.

“Nov 16th 2026 will be an unforgettable day here on as it’s the day I finally got recognised for my music and am officially a GRAMMY Nominee.”

— Devan Ekambaram, on Instagram

Announcing the nomination on Instagram, Ekambaram called it a special moment “because it’s the very 1st Tamil Song to ever be nominated and am so happy it’s a BHARATHIAR song,” and said he was thrilled to receive his first nomination “alongside legends like Angélique Kidjo and Pharrell Williams & Shakira and Burna Boy.”

Two musicians, two journeys

Ekambaram grew up in the United States and was studying engineering at the University of Illinois when a summer trip to India in 1995 set him on a different path. He secured a record deal in Chennai, and his debut album caught the attention of composer A. R. Rahman. He made his playback singing debut in 1999 with “Oh Maria” in Rahman’s Kadhalar Dhinam, and has since sung in more than 500 film soundtracks across Tamil and other South Indian languages, making his debut as a film composer in 2010. He has been creating independent Tamil music since 1998.

Susha began her training in Carnatic classical music, then studied jazz at the University of Toronto; her work combines Indian melodic traditions with jazz improvisation and contemporary sounds. In 2019 she was selected among the top 24 artistes for NEXA Music, an initiative by A. R. Rahman and Clinton Cerejo to mentor independent English-language musicians, and she released her debut album, Love Language, in August 2026.

The competition

The Best Global Music Performance field is heavyweight. “Varuvaaiy” is up against five-time Grammy winner Angélique Kidjo, featuring Pharrell Williams and Quavo, for “Bando (Orchestral)”; Rosalía and Dougie F for “Porcelana”; Shakira and Burna Boy for “Dai Dai”; and KerreKe, Mireya Ramos and Alex E Chávez for “Una Flor En Cada Estrella,” PTI reported.

Another Indian thread in the nominations

“Varuvaaiy” is not the only Indian connection on the list. The Mountain, the album by British virtual band Gorillaz, features contributions from several Indian musicians, including sitarist Anoushka Shankar, flautist Ajay Prasanna, singer Asha Bhosle and sarod players Amaan and Ayaan Ali Bangash. British singer-songwriter RAYE leads the 2027 nominations overall with 11, followed by Rosalía with nine.

When and where

The 69th Grammy Awards take place on Sunday, February 7, 2027, at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles. Whatever the outcome, the nomination itself is the landmark: a self-released Tamil devotional song, built on a poem written during the freedom struggle, now sits on the same shortlist as some of the biggest names in global music.
nri_angle: An Indian American composer’s Tamil bhajan reaching the Grammys’ global shortlist is a first for Tamil music and a landmark for the diaspora’s Carnatic tradition.
